seed: A turn has to say what it turns AROUND. A bell that swings hangs from its mount, not from its middle: put the pivot in the middle and the top swings one way while the bottom swings the other, which reads as a bobblehead. So this walk adds a Rotation, checks that a pivot arrives with it sitting on the middle of the layer with a crosshair on the picture, DRAGS that crosshair up above the shape, and checks the drag was taken by the crosshair rather than by the shape it was sitting in the middle of. It then sets the same point by name from the Around menu and by typing two numbers, because those are the three ways in and they all write one value.

steps.note: a Rotation, and with it an Around row reading Its centre. The pivot is on the picture from the moment the turn exists rather than behind a field somebody has to know to go looking for.
THE PICTURE TO LOOK AT: this is the bobblehead. The shape swings about its own middle, so its top goes one way while its bottom goes the other. Nothing about the two angles is wrong. The pivot is.
one drag on the crosshair and the turn now turns about a point ABOVE the shape: a bell rather than a bobblehead.

THE TEST, and it is two claims in one. The Rotation is still on the layer, so what undo took back was the PIVOT MOVE rather than the motion, which means the drag really did make its own single step. And the Around row is back on Its centre, which means the press was taken by the CROSSHAIR rather than by the shape it was sitting in the middle of: had the shape taken it, the shape would have moved, its pivot would have travelled with it, and this row would have read Its centre the whole way through with nothing for undo to take back.
the second way in: the spots worth a name, for the times the top of the box is exactly where it hangs from
and the third: two numbers, for when a number is what you want rather than a drag. All three write the same value.
